entries.title: White et al., 1986, compilation
entries.content: This dataset is a compilation of multiple partially overlapping animals. The cells making up the somatic nervous system were reconstructed by White et al., 1986 and compiled by Varshney et al., 2011. The cells making up the pharyngeal nervous systems were reconstructed by Albertson and Thomson, 1976 and cleaned up by Nikhil Bhatla, developer of WormWeb.org. Non-neuronal cells were not annotated individually but are grouped by cell type (e.g. Body wall muscles).

entries.title: Witvliet et al., 2020, datasets 1-8
entries.content: Chemical synapses for all eight datasets were acquired from Witvliet et al., 2020. Chemical synapses were annotated independently by three annotators and only chemical synapses that at least two annotators agreed to were included in the final dataset. Gap junctions were not thoroughly annotated but have been provided by the authors for anyone interested. The gap junction annotation is by no means exhaustive, and should not be treated as such.

entries.title: White et al., 1986, JSH and N2U
entries.content: The two datasets were reconstructed by White et al., 1986 and compiled by Durbin, 1987. Individual muscle cells were not annotated by White et al., 1986. To allow comparison to other datasets, individual muscle cells (and synapses onto them) were annotated in scans of the original EM micrographs by the Zhen Lab. These synapses have been added to the datasets instead of the originally listed anonymous neuromuscular junctions.

entries.title: White et al., 1986, JSE
entries.content: The dataset was reconstructed by White et al., 1986 and compiled by Hall and Russell, 1991.

connectionTypes.title: Types of Connection
connectionTypes.description: Nemanode catalogs several types of neural connections:

types.title: Chemical Synapses
types.description: Directional connections where neurotransmitters are released from a presynaptic cell to affect a postsynaptic cell. These are the most common type of connection in the C. elegans connectome.

types.title: Gap Junctions
types.description: Electrical synapses that allow direct communication between cells. These connections are bidirectional and allow for rapid signal transmission.

types.title: Neuromuscular Junctions
types.description: Specialized chemical synapses between neurons and muscle cells, essential for controlling movement.

downloadData.title: Download Data
downloadData.description: All datasets are available for download in multiple formats:

formats.title: CSV Format
formats.description: Comma-separated values format, suitable for spreadsheet applications and basic data analysis.

formats.title: JSON Format
formats.description: JavaScript Object Notation format, ideal for web applications and programmatic access.

formats.title: GraphML Format
formats.description: XML-based format for graphs, suitable for network analysis software.

apiAccess.title: API Access
apiAccess.description: Programmatic access to the data is available through our REST API. See the documentation for details.

contribute.title: How to Contribute
contribute.description: We welcome contributions from researchers and developers to help improve Nemanode. There are several ways you can contribute:

sections.title: Data Contributions
sections.content: If you have new datasets or improvements to existing ones, please submit them following our data format guidelines. All contributions will be reviewed by our team before integration.

sections.title: Code Contributions
sections.content: Nemanode is an open-source project. You can contribute to our codebase by submitting pull requests on our GitHub repository. Please make sure to follow our coding standards and include appropriate tests.

sections.title: Documentation
sections.content: Help us improve our documentation by suggesting edits or additions. Clear documentation is essential for making Nemanode accessible to new users.

submissionProcess.title: Submission Process
submissionProcess.content: Please email your contributions to contributions@nemanode.org or submit them through our GitHub repository.
